« Mon objectif, c’est » : de l’argent en: “My goal is”: extra money on top of what I set aside, the money I’ll have in total, or what I’ll earn from now on. Then “Money set aside, expenses, deadline”: the money I set aside, the purchases to pay before my goal, what I spend each session (consumables, ammo…) and “I want to get there in (days)”. Also “Which activity gets me to my goal fastest?”, “What if the number moves by 20%?” and “Compare with a saved calculation”. At the bottom of “Money set aside, expenses, deadline”, “I resell what I already own” adds to what you have the resale prices entered in My purchases for what you own (simulated resale). And under “My assumptions”, “My extra assumptions”: healing, fines, money lost on death or arrest, passive income, bonus, splitting among players, the money of one character only, all unchecked at first.
Le sens de ton but change la cible : « e: What your goal means changes the target: “on top of what I set aside” adds your reserve, “in total” counts it in, “from now on” doesn’t count what you already have. Purchases to pay first and what you spend each session add time. With a deadline, the answer says whether you’ll make it and, if not, how much more you’d need to play or earn. With “My extra assumptions” (Expert mode), healing, fines and money lost on death or arrest are added to your expenses per session, and passive income is added to your earnings per hour (at most its maximum stock per session). Example: 100 health points lost per session and a heal that restores 25 points for $500, so $2,000 of healing per session; with $100,000 per hour and 1 h sessions, you move forward at $98,000 per hour. These are examples, not game figures.
Une activité écartée l’est avec sa raiso: An activity that gets ruled out always comes with its reason: not enough players, missing starting purchase, too long for your time, or it costs more than it earns. Your share applies only once (players don’t split the reward again) and an activity only pays once it’s finished. With “My extra assumptions” (Expert mode): the bonus raises each reward (example: 50% more, $25,000 counts as $37,500); the equal split counts 100 ÷ number of players for a multiplayer mission (example: 4 players, 25%); when you count the money of one character only, a mission played only with the other one is ruled out, and the calculator says so.
Les hypothèses en plus du mode Expert co: The extra assumptions from Expert mode count here too: bonus, equal split and the money of one character only change your missions; healing, fines, death and arrest are added to the expenses taken off each session for the sessions you have left.
Un achat qui en demande un autre n’est j: A purchase that requires another one is never placed before it; a shared requirement is paid only once; a loop (A requires B, which requires A) blocks the calculation and says why. If a price is missing, the answer says “Path to complete” instead of assuming 0. “What matters in this calculation” tells you which goal the order serves and how many orders were compared (“All possible sequences… were compared”, or the search limit beyond 6 purchases). The simulated expenses per session and the passive income from “My extra assumptions” (Expert mode) count in the net earnings per hour used for waiting.
Un prix inconnu n’est jamais compté à 0: An unknown price is never counted as 0: the total becomes “at most” or “to complete”, and the answer says what’s missing. What you can pay today and what you can keep up over time (costs each session) are shown separately. With a number of sessions entered, the simulated expenses per session and the passive income from “My extra assumptions” (Expert mode) also go into your money session after session.
Tout s’affiche en plus : chaque partie a: Everything else shows up too: each session with its missions, earnings, and purchases, “What order should I buy them in?” (let the calculator choose, your order, what pays off fastest, the cheapest, straight to your goal, dipping into the money set aside), “What if…?”, “What changes everything”, the curve of your money with your real results, the calendar, “My plan variants” (keep this plan before trying something else), the formula, and “All the numbers in the calculation”. On the curve, you can fix a real point in one click; in “What if the number moves by 20%?”, clicking −20% or +20% uses that number. In “What matters to you”, five extra settings, all unchecked at first: “Also count my extra assumptions”, “Count the failed attempts from My assumptions”, “Count offline income between two sessions” (with a cap per break if you want), “Resell my purchases before the goal once I reach it” (with “I resell it after my goal” on each purchase before the goal) and, when you count the money of one character only, “Played by” on each mission.
Un déblocage ne se fait qu’une fois et u: An unlock only happens once and a purchase you need first is only paid for once; the time it takes to get it counts. “Lowest point” shows when you have the least money. If a must-have number is missing, the answer says “Path to complete” and tells you what to enter. If no plan keeps your money set aside, the plan is blocked and explains what to do: choose “As fast as possible” (the plan then dips into the money set aside and says so at every step) or change what you keep set aside. With no session duration, the path waits for the most profitable mission instead of starting just any mission, and it tells you if it leaves a mission out to go faster. The ammo you simulate in Expert mode is added to the fees of each attempt. Planned, started, and done are separate: “started” counts for nothing, only “done” (or a session you actually logged) changes the calculation, and the same session is never counted twice. Failed attempts: with 2 failed attempts out of 10, a mission you can redo earns 80% of its reward on average (example: $25,000 counts as $20,000); a mission done only once costs and lasts 1.25 times as much on average (you start it again until it succeeds); 10 out of 10 is refused. Offline income: what your owned purchases earn per hour keeps coming in during the break between two sessions (example: $2,000 per hour, 1 h sessions every day, 23 h break, so $46,000, or less with a cap per break). Resale: $40,000 entered on a garage bought for $80,000 gives $40,000 more at the end and a net cost of $40,000; the time to reach the goal doesn’t change. These are examples, not game figures.
C’est quoi « Mes hypothèses en plus » da: What is “My extra assumptions” in the calculator?
En mode Expert, « Mes hypothèses en plus: In Expert mode, “My extra assumptions” (just below “My assumptions”) lets you simulate what Rockstar hasn’t put numbers on: healing, fines, money lost on death or arrest (added to your expenses per session), passive income with its maximum stock (added to your earnings per hour), a bonus on mission rewards, an equal split among players and the money of one character only (Jason or Lucia). Everything is unchecked at first: nothing changes until you check something, and every number you choose stays marked “simulation”. The business plan uses them if you check “Also count my extra assumptions”.
Comment compter les soins, les amendes o: How do I count healing, fines or money lost on death?
Rockstar n’a publié ni prix de soin, ni: Rockstar hasn’t published any healing price, fine, or money lost on death or arrest for GTA VI. In the calculator (Expert mode, “My extra assumptions”), you can simulate them: healing = health lost per session ÷ health restored by one heal × price of one heal; fines, death, arrest = number per session × amount. The total is added to your expenses per session in My goal, My play time, What should I buy first? and My budget. Example: 100 health points lost per session and a heal that restores 25 points for $500, so $2,000 per session. These are examples, not game figures.
Comment compter un revenu passif dans le: How do I count passive income in the calculator?
Aucun revenu d’entreprise, stock ou plaf: No business income, stock or cap has been published for GTA VI. In Expert mode, in “My extra assumptions”, check “Passive income” and enter what it earns per hour of play and its maximum stock. It’s added to your earnings per hour (My goal “bit by bit”, What should I buy first?, My budget); in sessions, it earns at most its stock per session. In the business plan, “Count offline income between two sessions” also adds what your owned purchases earn during the break, with a cap per break if you want. It all stays a simulation.
Comment compter un bonus ou partager une: How do I count a bonus or split a reward among players?
En mode Expert, dans « Mes hypothèses en: In Expert mode, in “My extra assumptions”: “Bonus” adds a percentage to each mission reward (example: with 50%, $25,000 counts as $37,500); “Split each reward equally among the players” counts 100 ÷ number of players for a multiplayer mission (example: 4 players, 25%), without changing the share you entered. A share published by Rockstar is never replaced. None of this is confirmed in GTA VI.
